Your first hour, minute by minute
No surprises includes the schedule
Tea, water or nothing. Paperwork already done online if you chose.
The chat: history, worries, goals. Chair reclines exactly zero degrees.
The look: exam, photos, x-rays if needed, narrated in plain words.
The plan: findings and fees on paper, questions answered twice if useful.
You leave with a plan and zero commitments made under bright lights.
Before you ask
The waiting-room questions
Does it hurt?
Our whole operating theory is that it shouldn't. Numbing is checked before work starts, and a raised hand pauses everything, no questions asked.
I haven't been in years. Will I get told off?
No. The lecture is not a clinical instrument. You'll get a plan, not a guilt trip; we're genuinely just glad you came.
Can I bring my kid to my appointment?
Please do. Ride-along visits are how small people learn the chair is boring, in the best way.
Do you do payment plans?
Yes, interest-free over 6 or 10 months on anything over $300, arranged at the desk in two minutes.
Toothache reading this at 2am?
Call the out-of-hours line. A dentist answers, talks you through tonight, and books you tomorrow's first slot.
